newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin slams U.S. "hegemony" at Denver summit.
newsitem.headline: Jospin slams U.S. "hegemony" at Denver summit.

text.p: Socialist French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin attacked on Tuesday what he called the United States' drive for hegemony at last weekend's Denver Group of Seven industrial powers' summit.

The new prime minister, who did not attend the summit at which France was represented by conservative President Jacques Chirac, told parliament at question time: "I am not satisfied with the results of Denver...We see a certain tendency towards hegemony, which is not necessarily identical with exercising a great power's global responsibilities, even if it is a friend."
Jospin said Europe did not have the same social model as the United States and had always tried to maintain a balance between economics and social priorities.
"It will be up to Europe, and to France's own ability -- and my government will work to that end -- to ensure that Europe's concerns carry greater weight next time," he said.

The prime minister did not directly criticise Chirac's performance at the summit, saying he had not attended himself because he was not interested in "formal representative roles" and that Socialist finance and foreign ministers had accompanied the president "because we did not want him to be alone".

In Denver, Chirac rejected attempts to apply the American model of economic deregulation and welfare reduction to solve Europe's problem of high unemployment and slow growth, saying he remained attached to the European social model.
